Senses.Note: One corpus label with context-dependent appraisal: criticism, a mocked self-designation, and wall-facing imagery are all attested.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X70/X70n1382.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Wuzhun: Wuzhun Shifan bears the exact headword. Wuzhun says Cheng adopted Dry Chan as a self-name and calls that too a nail in empty space.
Source record (J/J26/J26nB177.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Poshan: Poshan Haiming bears the exact headword. Poshan criticizes merely sitting a few days of dry Chan as a limited attainment.
Source record (J/J27/J27nB198.xml). In his authored answer to a layman, Shiyu Mingfang uses dry Chan critically for sinking into emptiness and guarding stillness.

Source record (J/J29/J29nB223.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Wanshou: Wanshou Xingzheng bears the exact headword. Wanshou warns that a wavering, half-present condition must fall into dry Chan and silent illumination.
Source record (J/J38/J38nB425.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Guangshou: Guangshou Zhengyuan bears the exact headword. Guangshou labels wordless, speechless withdrawal small-vehicle dry Chan.

Senses.Explanation: Dry Chan is one label whose appraisal changes with context. Poshan, Wanshou, Guangshou, and Shiyu use it critically for limited sitting, guarding stillness, or speechless withdrawal. Wuzhun reports Cheng adopting it as a self-name while mocking that adoption, whereas Xutang deploys it for Bodhidharma-style wall-facing in contrast with public office. The entry therefore records the label and its attested appraisals rather than treating every occurrence as inert cultivation.
